name: generative-art
title: Generative art: a harmonograph that changes every minute
summary: A slowly turning harmonograph drawn over an AGSL nebula, with fireflies carried by a vortex flow field. The figure is picked from the minute of the day, and over the last ten seconds of each minute it fades into the next. The nebula's hue drifts through the day.
prompt: Make a piece of generative art for a phone or a frame: an evolving shader background, particles drifting in a flow field and a spirograph-like curve that slowly turns and becomes a different figure every minute. Gallery-worthy, and different every time you look.
hand_built: A single canvas of maths: one AGSL shader, one particle system and two parametric paths. The component library has nothing for any of the three.
teaches: The figure is two rotating phasors, x = cx + R·e^(−0.02a)·(0.62·cos(a + p1) + 0.38·cos(a(n + d) + p2)), with y the same using sin. The integer n gives |n − 1| lobes. The small detune d makes the loops precess and fill the rose, and the damping spirals it inward. One pathExpression of 900 points over a = 0…24π draws it

Different every minute without jumping: nA comes from seed(m·3 + 1, rand()) with m = timeInMin(), and nB is the next minute's value. Both figures are drawn, crossfaded with fade = smooth_step(continuousSec() % 60, 60, 50), and the second figure is drawn only while fade > 0 (conditionalOperations)
A clock that moves smoothly all day: T = timeInHr()·3600 + continuousSec(). continuousSec() alone restarts every hour, which would make the phases jump

A flow field with no clumping: velocities from a stream function, vx = −k·sin(x·fx + k1)·sin(y·fy − k2), vy = −k·cos(x·fx + k1)·cos(y·fy − k2). This flow is divergence-free (Taylor-Green vortices). fx = 4π/W and fy = 4π/H make the field tile, so particles can wrap round the edges with %
Particles that never pop: each one has its own life and age = (age + 1) % life. It respawns at a random point (ifElse(rand()·W, …, age − 0.5)) exactly when its alpha, square(sin(π·age/life)), is 0

The glow is the same path stroked three times (7, 2.6 and 0.9 px at alpha 0.07, 0.22 and 0.9) with a sweep gradient. Eighteen beads ride the curve: the same formula evaluated in a loop at u = 75.4·fract(i/18 + T·0.003)

The AGSL background domain-warps uv three times with time-driven sines and mixes two cosine palettes. Its hue uniform is 0.62 + T·0.00004, so the colour drifts through the day. A vignette keeps the edges dark

Four looks. Dark is the nebula with pastel lines. Light lays a themed cream wash (@colors.wash: 84% cream in light, transparent in dark) over the same shader, so it reads as tinted paper, and the lines, sparks, beads and caption switch to deep inks through themed colours: the sweep gradient takes @colors refs. Mono ({"$if": "theme.mono"}) drops the shader, particles and glow: the figure is one hairline in onSurface with six dots, its phases from the minute (p1m = m·0.9), so an always-on screen repaints once a minute
pitfalls: Shader support: the AGSL nebula plays on Android 13+ (AGSL), in the C++/Skia player (SkRuntimeEffect) and in the TypeScript web player in a browser (transpiled to WebGL2). The headless TypeScript render (players/typescript/render.mjs) has no WebGL, so it stops at the shader with 'document is not defined'. Check the TypeScript side in a browser page instead (package_web)
A particle document needs frames: render with duration (and a seed) or the fireflies are still where they were seeded
Particle initialValues cannot read another particle variable ("rand() * @life" is refused: unknown token): give each its own expression
Keep each expression within Android's 32 entries: the figure formula is 26, so the frequencies and phases (nA, d, p1, p2) are separate named variables

rc-inspect's audit reports dead_code for k1, k2, fx, fy and the shader's hue uniform. They are read only by particle equations and a shader uniform, which the inspector does not count as reads (I18). The renders show them working
The ratio label switches figure at the middle of the crossfade (ifElse(nA, nB, fade − 0.5))

Resource variables are always written, even if only one look uses them (unlike canvas `variable`s, which are written at first use). The look-specific ones (T, fade, p1, k1, nB…) are declared at the top of the light/dark branch, so the mono documents carry no continuousSec() and do not repaint every frame
A paint `alpha` after a `color` replaces that colour's own alpha. Set a translucent themed colour without a following alpha op

snippets.note: AGSL nebula: three domain warps, two cosine palettes, vignette; uniforms iResolution, iTime = @T, uHue
180 fireflies: per-particle life and age, a divergence-free vortex field, wrap round and respawn at alpha 0
the harmonograph of the current minute, 900 points
crossfade over the last ten seconds of each minute
mono: the figure as one hairline in onSurface with six dots, its phases moving once a minute

check.describe: Dark nebula (violet, blue, teal or rose depending on the hour) with a glowing pastel harmonograph in the centre, beads on it, and warm firefly sparks drifting in swirls; a small centred caption 'Nº 0848 · 7-fold' at the bottom (edition = minute of the day + 1, and the figure's symmetry). 14:08 shows a different figure (3-fold); at :56 both figures are visible mid-crossfade; at 21:42 the figure and hue differ again. Resized, the figure stays centred at 0.4 × the short side and the particles fill the whole box. Light: cream paper with a faint tint of the nebula, deep-ink lines (indigo, teal, rose, ochre) and dark sparks. Mono-dark: a white hairline rose on black with a grey caption, no particles. Mono-light: the same in black on white.

java_difference: json2rc writes 8 bytes fewer: after a paint with an AGSL runtime shader, {"shader": 0} becomes one PaintBundle SHADER 0 in json2rc and two in Java's parser (a minimal case: Java 249 B, json2rc 241 B). Both clear the shader, so the documents behave the same
